name: OK-04
label: Safe R

model.rationale: Tom Cole is a well-funded long-time incumbent in an R+17 district, while Mitchell Jacob has raised under $70K with minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets price Cole at 97%, and no polling or expert ratings suggest any vulnerability.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending surge for the challenger or a scandal involving Cole could narrow the race, though neither is in evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+17. Tom Cole, a veteran incumbent, is running for reelection with a large financial advantage: he has raised roughly $3.8 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, plus modest outside support. His Democratic opponent, Mitchell Jacob, has raised about $65,000 with little cash remaining, and an independent candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Cole about a 97% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes Cole a heavy favorite, with the Democratic challenger facing steep odds in a district that has consistently favored Republicans by wide margins.
